result:
I've built the workbook at `extraction/meredith.xlsx`. It has the four sheets in order (Deal ledger with 85 rows, Rounds, Questions with 11 entries, Deal facts), each with a frozen header, filters, wrapped text and real MM/DD/YYYY dates. A script confirmed that every quotation appears word for word in the filing, is 30 words or fewer and carries its printed page. It also confirmed that Sort dates never go backwards and that every bid row has All cash, Formality and Conditions filled.

## How the sale went
Meredith first tried to sell only four TV stations. From 11/16/2020 its banker, Moelis, contacted 20 parties, and 17 signed confidentiality agreements. In round 1, four parties bid for stations. Gray, Party A and Party B also indicated interest in the whole local-TV business (LMG), to be bought after Meredith spun off its magazine and digital business (NMG) to shareholders.

Round 2 took final station bids, with some arriving a day late, on 01/25–26/2021. On 01/28/2021 the board paused the station sale and switched to selling LMG. Round 3, opened 03/17/2021, asked Gray and Party B for final LMG offers. Party D, an investment firm that had come back uninvited on 03/11/2021, was admitted on 03/30/2021 with a cash-plus-stock proposal.

On 04/23/2021 the board chose Gray and dropped Party B. It signed with Gray on 05/03/2021 at $14.51 cash per share plus the spun-off NMG shares. Party D's unsolicited offers after signing pushed Gray to $16.99 per share in an amendment signed 06/02/2021. It is one process with three rounds, and the post-signing contest is recorded as post.

## Questions and my recommendations
- **Q1, how the sale divides into rounds:** keep one process and three rounds. The best alternative would start a new round at the 01/28/2021 switch to LMG. Nothing meets the tests for a second process. The only gaps of two months or more with no buyer contact are before the process and after signing.
- **Q2, who signed confidentiality agreements:** treat Parties A–D as among the 17 signers, which leaves exactly 12 unnamed signers who never bid.
- **Q3, Q5, Q9, deadline outcomes:** round 1, Enforced. Round 2, Late bids accepted. Round 3, Extended and then Enforced.
- **Q4, prices:** leave price cells blank wherever the filing gives only enterprise values. Also keep Party D's per-share cash dividend figures out of the price cells, because they leave out its stock component.
- **Q6, how Parties A, C and D left round 2:** Party A did not submit an LMG proposal. Parties C and D were dropped when the station sale paused. Party D re-entered on 03/11/2021.
- **Q7, Party D's Morris Trust proposals:** these are whole-company bids, not all cash.
- **Q8, Party D's partners:** Party E and Party B's financing affiliate are supporters of Party D, not a bidding group.
- **Q10, Party D's bids:** Formal with Heavy conditions from 04/15/2021, because Party D submitted markups of the merger agreement.
- **Q11, after signing:** record Gray's later offers as Formal bids. Record the 06/02 amendment and its 06/03 announcement as Other material event rather than a second signing.

## Limits
- **Enterprise values:** most LMG bids before signing are stated only as enterprise values, so they have no per-share price. I did not convert them.
- **Amendment:** there is no event label for an amended merger agreement, so the 06/02 amendment is recorded as Other material event (Q11).
- **Dotdash sale:** the 10/06/2021 sale of the spun-off NMG company to Dotdash (IAC) is only in Deal facts. The conventions allow no post-signing row for it.
- **Media reports:** the filing mentions media reports only once, undated, in the board's reasons. That row is placed just before signing.
- **Individual dates missing:** confidentiality agreement dates and the station bid prices in round 1 are not given individually, so those cells are windows or left blank.
